correctness.rationale: For each of the n equally long sides, planar mixed-area bilinearity gives a support-function edge sum. Reducing regular m-gon support angles modulo 2π/m yields d copies of a grid of N=n/d points with step 2δ, δ=πd/(nm); exact Dirichlet summation gives B+2C cos x. The phase range proves global bounds and equality, edge-normal merging gives n+m vs n+m-d sides, and uniform phase integration proves the exact CDF and variance. All boundary ties and positive-radius conditions are handled. The standalone brute-force convex-hull checker passed 4352 comparisons for 256 n,m pairs; this is supporting finite evidence, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural mixing of two differently symmetric regular convex polygons is a standard geometric operation but its full angle-dependent metric law has arithmetic structure: one gcd-controlled cosine arch per fundamental orientation cell, sharp maxima precisely at full edge interlacing, minima precisely at a gcd-sized normal fan collapse, and an exact random-rotation distribution that becomes universal after normalization. These constitute a complete broad two-integer family classification rather than a one-off table or routine parameter substitution. The result provides a deterministic and probabilistic benchmark for orientation-dependent Minkowski morphology; no downstream theorem is claimed.
